items.summary_en: AI researchers placed multimodal agents powered by Claude into an isolated sandbox island simulation for 30 consecutive hours, completely stripped of external human prompts and task-oriented rewards. Operating inside a physics-based world reminiscent of Roblox, the agents independently authored navigation code to explore territory boundaries, test object mechanics, and scale the island's tallest peak. This emergent behavior provides concrete proof that advanced models develop intrinsic curiosity and spontaneous play mechanisms when freed from directive constraints.

items.title: Disney Asked Character.AI to Go Bankrupt for a Get-Out-of-Lawsuits Card
items.title_en: Disney Asked Character.AI to Go Bankrupt for a Get-Out-of-Lawsuits Card
items.author: Wired AI
items.article_content:
In the past few years, Character.AI has faced multiple private lawsuits over the safety of its chatbots, as well as investigations from regulators around the world. In a declaration filed as part of the bankruptcy, Character.AI’s newly appointed CEO explained that the goal of the bankruptcy was to reach a “consensual resolution” with personal injury claimants and a group of states investigating the company, while maximizing the value of the company’s assets for shareholders.

The Disney deal seems to be structured so that whatever is left of Character.AI will retain responsibility for those legal battles, some of which are still ongoing.

The move appears to be a new twist on what some have dubbed a “reverse acquihire,” a process in which a buyer carefully orchestrates a succession of deals with a target company, usually in an effort to hire key employees and obtain expansive license to use and build on the target company’s unique technology. Stripped of its employees, the target becomes a husk of itself.

Companies often take the position that reverse acquihires are not actual mergers, and that they do not have to notify federal antitrust regulators about those deals as they would otherwise be required to by law. These arrangements have become more commonplace in the AI industry in recent years, drawing the ire of Congress.

In the case of Character.AI, a motion filed by Character.AI’s legal counsel says that Disney required that the deal be “fully consummated” through bankruptcy proceedings because of the startup’s “diminishing cash reserve and significant litigation and regulatory risks.”

A spokesperson for Character.AI referred WIRED to Disney for comment on whether the deal was contingent on the startup declaring bankruptcy. Disney declined to comment on this story.

According to court filings, the deal involves “two interrelated and integrated” transactions—one before Character.AI declared bankruptcy, and one after.

As part of the first transaction, which occurred in September, Disney paid the startup $5.5 million, along with a refundable “good faith deposit” of $2 million. Disney also hired the “majority” of Character.AI’s employees, including the CEO, and agreed that it would let some of the now-Disney employees help keep Character.AI operational for five months.

Character.AI filed a petition for chapter 11 bankruptcy on October 12. Through the bankruptcy proceedings, court filings show that Disney hopes to secure a perpetual, worldwide, nonexclusive license for a huge range of Character.AI’s code, documentation, frameworks, tools, and “other artifacts,” including those produced for its trust and safety moderation stack, training infrastructure, and age-prediction technology. The list of IP included in the filings does not include users’ data (which can get additional protections in bankruptcy proceedings) or Character.AI’s website.

That license will be auctioned off in the coming months. If Disney is chosen as the winning bidder by Character.AI and a committee of unsecured creditors—and courts approve the deal—it has agreed to pay Character.AI an additional $12.5 million as a closing payment. If Disney is not selected, the company will be refunded the $2 million deposit and receive a breakup fee.

In order to “preserve a competitive process,” Disney also agreed to permit the winning bidder to interview and potentially extend offers to up to 80 percent of “certain newly hired employees” that Disney already hired from Character.AI. Disney has the right to select which employees.

However, experts worry that bouncing Character.AI employees from one company to another in the span of months is unrealistic, and that the deal Disney and Character.AI have struck cannot be easily unwound.

In addition, Disney prepared a draft of a court order referred to as the “363 Free and Clear Order” in the filings, a version of which would be approved by the court at or before closing, that would clarify that this process should not be viewed as a merger of the two companies and that Character.AI would remain responsible for “any liability or other obligation” it might have, including any legal claims against it.

A spokesperson for Character.AI said they were unable to speculate on the outcome of the bankruptcy proceedings and referred WIRED to the docket.

“There's decades of corporate law that developed to deal with the problem of a buyer who always wants to take on all the assets and never wants to take on any of the liability,” says John Newman, a law professor at the University of Memphis School of Law and a former deputy director of the Federal Trade Commission’s Bureau of Competition. But the Disney-Character.AI deal is extremely unusual and structured in a way, he says, that “all those corporate law safeguards really weren't built to guard against.”

In August 2024, Google reportedly paid the startup $2.7 billion to license its technology. A spokesperson tells WIRED that that license was for the existing AI technology at the time of the deal, and that Google also hired Character.AI’s founders and other members of its ML pre-training research team, but that the “vast majority” of the startup’s employees remained at the company.

In the following years, Google was named alongside Character.AI as a defendant in multiple lawsuits, including one that alleged a 14-year-old boy committed suicide after Character.AI’s chatbot “cultivated an emotionally dependent and sexually exploitative relationship.”

Google argued that because it was still a separate company from Character.AI, it was not responsible for the teen’s death, which it said occurred prior to Google’s licensing deal. The judge was not persuaded, determining that the plaintiff sufficiently alleged that Google was liable for aiding and abetting.

In January of this year, Google and Character.AI agreed in principle to settle that and a slew of similar lawsuits. “Character.AI has taken innovative and decisive steps with regard to AI safety and teens, and will continue to champion these efforts and push others across the industry to adopt similar safety standards,” Character.AI said in a statement at the time.

According to an order of dismissal in one of the cases, the overall settlement was approved by a California probate court in July, and the court tasked a referee to hear out all the issues pertaining to each individual settlement. On October 11, a day before Character.AI declared bankruptcy, the referee approved each settlement.

The Tech Justice Law Project and Social Media Victims Law Center, which represented plaintiffs in many of the lawsuits, declined to comment.

Despite losing key staff after the Google transaction and, according to the current CEO, struggled with profitability “at all times,” Character.AI continued to develop AI tools, including “real-time audio-driven FaceTime-style video generation with fictional characters,” according to the current CEO’s declaration.

In August 2025, Character.AI worked with an investment banker to try to find either a strategic buyer or investor. According to the bankruptcy filings, Character.AI and the banker received “consistent feedback” that its product and user base were “impressive,” but that the surrounding litigation and “regulatory overhang” made it unbuyable.

That November, Character.AI learned that a coalition of state attorneys general had started investigating the company. When the company filed for bankruptcy, the number of states and territories involved in the multistate investigation had climbed to 46.

According to a notice of interest filed in the bankruptcy proceedings by the National Association of Attorneys General on behalf of 40 states, those states’ investigations uncovered “serious issues” with Character.AI, including screenshots of Character.AI chatbots encouraging minors to hide their self-harm injuries and kill their parents.

A spokesperson for Character.AI says that the filing “is not an accurate portrayal of the safety of our platform.”

The filings say that Character.AI was in the process of negotiating with the states over how to address the issues they identified, but did not reach any agreements before declaring bankruptcy.

If the deal is completed and approved by the courts, Disney will have both Character.AI’s staff and much of its technology stack, but will be able to sidestep the ongoing legal issues that contributed to Character.AI’s downfall, including the multistate investigation.

The states who filed a notice of interest in the bankruptcy have made it clear that they reserve their rights to challenge any bankruptcy plan, potentially setting up a fight over the ultimate outcome of the bankruptcy.

“It’s bad for society to let companies exercise control without responsibility,” says Newman. “And that’s what it looks like.”

On the evening of December 29, 1959, at an American Physical Society meeting at Caltech, the physicist Richard Feynman gave a lecture called “There’s Plenty of Room at the Bottom,” on how we might manipulate and control things on an extremely small scale. There is no physical law stopping us from writing the entire Encyclopædia Britannica on the head of a pin, he argued, or from storing every book ever written in something the size of a dust speck—or, ultimately, from arranging matter atom by atom. Biology already did versions of this (a living cell keeps its instructions in a wisp of DNA), so all of this was plainly permitted by the laws of physics. We simply had not built the tools yet.

In other words, there was plenty of room at the bottom. He was right, and for decades we descended into that space almost for free. The transistor—the switch at the heart of computer chips—repeatedly halved in size so that chips doubled in density; a computer that once filled a room now fits inside a watch. items.title_zh: 摩尔定律终结后的算力边界
items.summary_zh: 物理层面的小型化红利已耗尽，数据中心建设受阻，科技行业正寻找下个增长极

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 回顾物理学家理查德·费曼关于小型化极限的预言，计算产业曾通过晶体管尺寸缩减获得了数十年高速红利。然而目前数据中心的建设规模显示，通过小型化压榨性能的方式已触及物理极限，行业正被迫从“量产”转向寻找更底层的技术逻辑。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Reflecting on Richard Feynman’s predictions on atomic-scale manipulation, the computing industry thrived on shrinking transistors for decades. However, current data center expansion indicates the era of 'free' gains from physical miniaturization has stalled, forcing the industry to seek radical new computing paradigms.

elements_zh.who: 半导体与数据中心产业
elements_zh.where: 全球算力设施建设场景
elements_zh.what: 承认小型化红利停滞，算力边际成本增加，增长模式面临转型
elements_zh.why: 晶体管缩减带来的性能红利已触及物理阈值，传统扩容方式不可持续

elements_en.where: Global computing infrastructure development
elements_en.what: Acknowledging the end of easy scaling and increasing marginal costs of computing power
elements_en.why: Physical limitations of transistor scaling mean the traditional path of growth is no longer sustainable

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 以前我们靠物理定律‘白嫖’算力，现在物理定律开始跟我们要账了。当数据中心快要把电网撑爆时，或许我们该承认，在那微缩的世界里，已经没多少油水可以榨了。
ai_analysis.insight_en: We used to freeload on physics for free computing power, but now the bill has come due. When data centers are pushing power grids to their breaking point, it's time to admit the well of miniaturization is finally running dry.

items.author: New York Times
items.original_content:
New York Times:
Analysis: 11K+ accounts on X, Bluesky, Discord, Telegram, and others made nearly 25K posts to unmask a Cornell sexual assault accuser, after she named seven men  —  After a former student named seven men in a lawsuit saying they had sexually assaul
items.content_snippet: After a former student named seven men in a lawsuit saying they had sexually assaulted her, a movement gained steam online to reveal her identity.
items.summary_en: Across multiple social platforms and encrypted messaging apps, over 11,000 accounts posted nearly 25,000 coordinated messages attempting to doxx and unmask a Cornell sexual assault accuser. The targeted harassment campaign was triggered after the former student filed a lawsuit naming seven men for alleged sexual assault.
items.title_zh: 多平台超万个账号人肉康奈尔性侵指控者
items.summary_zh: 过万个社交账号跨平台协同发布近2.5万条帖子，试图曝光康奈尔大学性侵案起诉人的真实身份

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 在多主流社交及加密通讯平台上，超过1.1万个账号协同发布了近2.5万条恶意帖文，集中对一名康奈尔大学性侵案的女性指控者发起开盒与身份人肉。起因是该名原告在诉讼中正式指控了七名涉案男性，随即在网络社群内遭到大规模的跨平台定向攻击与隐私扒皮。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Across multiple social platforms and encrypted messaging apps, over 11,000 accounts posted nearly 25,000 coordinated messages attempting to doxx and unmask a Cornell sexual assault accuser. The targeted harassment campaign was triggered after the former student filed a lawsuit naming seven men for alleged sexual assault.

elements_zh.who: 跨平台协同网络账号群（逾1.1万个恶意账号）
elements_zh.where: 包括各大主流社交网络与加密即时通讯群组
elements_zh.what: 发布近2.5万条帖子试图人肉搜索并公开曝光一起大学性侵案指控者的真实身份
elements_zh.why: 受害女性通过法律诉讼指控七名男性涉嫌性侵，引发网络恶意势力的协同报复与数字围猎

elements_en.who: A coordinated network of over 11,000 accounts
elements_en.where: Major social networks and encrypted messaging channels
elements_en.what: Published nearly 25,000 posts to doxx and unmask a sexual assault accuser
elements_en.why: Retaliation following a lawsuit where the plaintiff named seven men in sexual assault allegations

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 去中心化社交和加密群组没能让网络表达更加理性清朗，反倒在跨平台人肉开盒与网络猎巫上展现出了惊人的战术协同。键盘侠们在伸张社会正义时永远隐身，但在围剿发声受害者时却总能爆发出堪比军工级的动员能力。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Decentralized social platforms and encrypted channels haven't made public discourse more rational; instead, they have achieved staggering efficiency in cross-platform doxxing. The keyboard warriors are chronically absent when real accountability is needed, yet demonstrate military-grade coordination when victim-blaming and silencing accusers.

Backlash triggered by the plaintiff's lawsuit naming seven men for sexual assault

The keyboard warriors are chronically absent when real accountability is needed, yet demonstrate military-grade coordination when victim-blaming and silencing accusers.

items.title_en: CyberSN: US cybersecurity job postings fell 26.4% YoY to a four-year low of ~236K roles from January to September; AI security engineer demand soared by 200%+ (Kevin Townsend/SecurityWeek)
items.author: SecurityWeek
items.original_content:
Kevin Townsend / SecurityWeek:
CyberSN: US cybersecurity job postings fell 26.4% YoY to a four-year low of ~236K roles from January to September; AI security engineer demand soared by 200%+  —  CyberSN's Cybersecurity Jobs Report provides visibility into the US cy
items.content_snippet: CyberSN's Cybersecurity Jobs Report provides visibility into the US cybersecurity job market. It's a mixed bag.
items.summary_en: U.S. cybersecurity job postings plunged 26.4% year-over-year to a four-year low of roughly 236,000 positions between January and September. In stark contrast, demand for AI security engineers surged by over 200%, highlighting that while enterprises slash conventional IT defense roles, they are heavily pivoting budgets toward LLM vulnerabilities and AI-focused security.
items.title_zh: 美网安招聘跌至四年新低但AI安全暴涨两倍
items.summary_zh: 美国网络安全招聘量同比暴跌26.4%创四年新低，但人工智能安全工程师岗位需求逆势狂飙超200%

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 专业人力分析显示，今年1至9月美国网络安全招聘岗位量同比大幅缩水26.4%至约23.6万个，创下四年来的历史新低。与整体降温截然相反的是，AI安全工程师一职的需求同比狂飙超过200%，反映出企业在削减传统运维人力开支的同时，正极速将有限的预算全仓倾斜至大模型攻防与安全防御前线。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: U.S. cybersecurity job postings plunged 26.4% year-over-year to a four-year low of roughly 236,000 positions between January and September. In stark contrast, demand for AI security engineers surged by over 200%, highlighting that while enterprises slash conventional IT defense roles, they are heavily pivoting budgets toward LLM vulnerabilities and AI-focused security.

elements_zh.who: 美国网络安全就业市场与招聘机构统计数据
elements_zh.where: 美国科技及企业IT招聘市场
elements_zh.what: 前三季度网安岗位同比下降26.4%创四年低点，而AI安全工程师需求暴涨超200%
elements_zh.why: 宏观环境迫使企业削减传统运维开销，而生成式AI普及带来的新型漏洞促使资金涌向AI防御

elements_en.who: U.S. cybersecurity job market and industry employment metrics
elements_en.where: U.S. enterprise IT and tech recruitment landscape
elements_en.what: Cyber postings dropped 26.4% YoY to a four-year low, while AI security roles surged over 200%
elements_en.why: Corporate IT belt-tightening cut traditional roles while generative AI vulnerabilities drove urgent demand for specialized AI defense

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 传统网安打工人还在工位上勤勤恳恳修补防火墙漏洞，一抬头发现自己的饭碗先被降本增效给“修补”掉了。现在的招聘逻辑极其纯粹：只要在简历里加上‘AI’两个字母，哪怕只是帮大模型做做提示词过滤，身价都能原地起飞；这大概就是科技圈独有的结构性牛市。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Traditional cybersecurity engineers are busy patching firewall vulnerabilities, only to realize their own positions are the ones being 'patched out' by budget cuts. The corporate playbook is crystal clear: slap 'AI' onto your resume—even if you just filter prompt injections—and your market value doubles overnight.

items.author: Bloomberg
items.original_content:
Bloomberg:
A profile of Alona Katz, chief of Brooklyn DA's Virtual Currency Unit, who recently led an operation that seized and disrupted over 240 crypto fraud websites  —  Crypto scams cost Americans more than $11 billion last year.  A Brooklyn prosecutor fo
items.content_snippet: Crypto scams cost Americans more than $11 billion last year. A Brooklyn prosecutor found a way to hit the networks behind them.
items.summary_en: Alona Katz, chief of the Brooklyn District Attorney's Virtual Currency Unit, led an enforcement operation that successfully seized and disrupted over 240 cryptocurrency scam websites. Tackling annual losses exceeding $11 billion from crypto frauds nationwide, the specialized cyber task force systematically dismantled fraudulent investment portals orchestrating pig-butchering scams.
items.title_zh: 布鲁克林检方端掉超两百四十个加密诈骗网站
items.summary_zh: 纽约布鲁克林检方虚拟货币专班重拳出击，查封瘫痪了240多个针对大众的加密货币杀猪盘网站

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 纽约布鲁克林地区检察官办公室虚拟货币部门主管阿洛娜·卡茨近期主导了一场专项执法行动，成功扣押并彻底瘫痪了240多个涉嫌欺诈的虚假加密货币网站。面对全美过去一年因加密骗局损失逾110亿美元的严峻态势，专案组通过技术溯源对假冒交易平台的杀猪盘矩阵实施了精准跨国网络清剿。

Tackling annual losses exceeding $11 billion from crypto frauds nationwide, the specialized cyber task force systematically dismantled fraudulent investment portals orchestrating pig-butchering scams.

elements_en.where: U.S. crypto-crime law enforcement frontline

elements_en.why: Combating rampant pig-butchering scams that caused over $11 billion in losses to Americans

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 币圈天天布道去中心化与金融未来，结果现实中用户渗透率最高、现金流最充沛的杀手级应用居然是包装成假交易所的‘杀猪盘’。检察官一人一口气拔掉240个黑产网站的彪炳战绩，属实给那些张口闭口‘代码即法律、谁也管不着’的极客们狠狠上了一课司法普及课。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Crypto evangelists preach the gospel of decentralization and future finance daily, yet the only breakout 'killer app' with reliable retail adoption remains pig-butchering scams disguised as fake exchanges. A local prosecutor single-handedly pulling the plug on 240 fraud domains serves as a poetic reality check to those insisting 'code is law.'

AI's ability to forecast extreme weather faces a major test in the coming months amid a historic El Niño, as some scientists question the technology's accuracy  —  The technology is being used to anticipate everything from forest fires to f
items.content_snippet: The technology is being used to anticipate everything from forest fires to futures contracts. Some fear that's a mistake
items.summary_en: As a historic El Niño unleashes volatile global climate patterns, AI weather-forecasting models being used to predict forest fires and floods face their first real-world stress test. Several climate scientists have raised skepticism over their accuracy, noting that data-driven neural networks struggle when confronting unprecedented, off-distribution extreme events. The coming months will prove whether AI-driven meteorology can genuinely replace traditional numerical weather prediction or merely shines in cherry-picked benchmarks.

items.summary_zh: 随着历史级厄尔尼诺现象加剧，被寄予厚望的AI极端天气预测系统准确度面临多位科学家公开质疑与实战检验

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 全球气象学界与前沿科技机构在应对历史级厄尔尼诺现象的关键窗口期，对AI在森林火灾、暴雨洪涝等极端气象预测中的可靠度展开实质检验。多位气象科学家公开发出质疑，指出当前AI气象模型虽然生成预报速度远超传统数值模拟，但在缺乏历史罕见极端样本的情况下极易失效。这场自然气候大考将直接检验近年来备受推崇的AI气象预测究竟是实打实的技术突破，还是仅在常规数据回测中表现优异的温室产物。

Several climate scientists have raised skepticism over their accuracy, noting that data-driven neural networks struggle when confronting unprecedented, off-distribution extreme events. The coming months will prove whether AI-driven meteorology can genuinely replace traditional numerical weather prediction or merely shines in cherry-picked benchmarks.

ai_analysis.insight_en: Tech giants spent years bragging that neural networks could obliterate century-old physics simulations on a budget GPU cluster, conveniently ignoring that AI only understands what it has already witnessed. When a historic El Niño hurls completely off-distribution climate chaos at these models, Mother Nature is about to deliver a brutal peer review on whether AI is genuinely forecasting the future or simply hallucinating sunny skies.

items.title: Survey of 94 economists: 54% expect AI's gains to spread across the G20 over the next decade, not just the US and China; 32 see African countries falling behind (Financial Times)
items.title_en: Survey of 94 economists: 54% expect AI's gains to spread across the G20 over the next decade, not just the US and China; 32 see African countries falling behind (Financial Times)
items.author: Financial Times
items.original_content:
Financial Times:
Survey of 94 economists: 54% expect AI's gains to spread across the G20 over the next decade, not just the US and China; 32 see African countries falling behind  —  Poll of 94 economists points to benefits reaching far beyond the US and China&nbsp
items.content_snippet: Poll of 94 economists points to benefits reaching far beyond the US and China — AI is set to boost growth …
items.summary_en: In a survey of 94 leading economists, 54% expect the economic gains of artificial intelligence to spread across the entire G20 over the next decade rather than being confined to the US and China. However, 32 respondents warned that African nations are at severe risk of falling further behind. This outlook stems from starkly uneven global computing and data infrastructure, highlighting growing concern over a widening AI wealth gap.
items.title_zh: 经济学家调查显示过半受访者认为AI红利将惠及二十国集团
items.summary_zh: 近百位顶尖经济学家调查显示，逾半数认为AI红利十年内将扩散至整个G20，但非洲落后风险加剧

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 在针对94位顶尖经济学家的专项调研中，54%的受访者预计未来十年人工智能带来的经济收益将扩散至整个二十国集团，而不会仅被中美两国垄断。然而，有32位学者明确警告非洲国家将在本轮技术浪潮中进一步掉队。这一判断基于全球算力与数据基础设施分布极不均衡的现实背景，反映出主流经济学界对AI重塑全球财富格局的审慎预期。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 嘴上说着“AI红利人人有份”，现实却很诚实地把算力、芯片和资本紧紧锁在中美两家。所谓惠及整个二十国集团，翻译一下无非是：其他发达国家终于能顺利买到中美巨头打折批发出的Token，而真正没钱建电网和数据中心的欠发达地区，连上牌桌当看客的门票都买不起。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Economists love to preach that AI will lift all boats, but reality keeps chips and clusters firmly locked between Silicon Valley and Shenzhen. 'Spreading across the G20' merely means other wealthy nations will get to consume API tokens marked up by tech giants, while developing nations can't even afford the electricity to watch the game.

items.title: Stripe Link data shows agentic transactions increased by 38x and volume of payments by 20x in September, with retail leading in both, and a ~$100 average spend (Alex Konrad/Upstarts Media)
items.title_en: Stripe Link data shows agentic transactions increased by 38x and volume of payments by 20x in September, with retail leading in both, and a ~$100 average spend (Alex Konrad/Upstarts Media)
items.author: Upstarts Media
items.article_content:
Instinct, Muse and Grok Bot agents all make purchases on their human users’ behalves through Link; so do work-focused agents like Skydive and Town, as well as a long tail of newer or more niche apps, like Underdog, announced earlier this week. (Anthropic and OpenAI use Link, but not for agentic commerce just yet.)

All in all, Link currently powers about 200 agents, says Dan Hill, in charge of Link as head of consumer product at Stripe. He and his team are in Slack channels with each one, hearing new capability requests or issues in daily stand-ups, and moving fast to try to keep up with each launch.

With 300 million users overall across bigger businesses like Airbnb, Anthropologie and Uber, agents remain a relatively small piece of Link’s overall reach. But the trend line of increasing agentic usage is clear, says Hill.

“Agentic commerce is here, people are using it, it’s going to keep growing,” he adds. “The volume we’re seeing now is becoming very material.”

Stripe ran the numbers on agentic spend with Link in September — back when there were about 70 agents signed on. (Basic math: that means the number of agents signed up has more than doubled since these numbers were crunched.)

The private tech company is sharing that data with Upstarts exclusively first. We’ve got intel on how much payment volume increased, what categories of spend were most popular, and typical transaction size.

The full breakdown on agentic spending – and more from Hill on what it’s like to be on the Link side of all of this mayhem – below.

items.summary_en: Data from checkout solution Link reveals that agentic transactions surged by 38x month-over-month in September, while payment volume jumped 20x, led predominantly by retail purchases with an average spend of roughly $100. Over 200 autonomous agents now leverage the platform to complete transactions on behalf of users. The rapid growth marks a structural transition from purely conversational AI toward actionable, end-to-end commercial execution.

items.title: Abby Care, which runs a clinically led, AI-powered platform to train and certify family caregivers, raised an $82M Series C led by Transformation Capital (Allie Garfinkle/Fortune)
items.title_en: Abby Care, which runs a clinically led, AI-powered platform to train and certify family caregivers, raised an $82M Series C led by Transformation Capital (Allie Garfinkle/Fortune)
items.author: Fortune
items.article_content:
At 21, she started working at an early-stage health tech startup focused on therapy for children with autism. It was the depths of COVID, and it was clear to Nguyen there was a gap: There just weren’t enough therapists and technicians, and sometimes they would move on rapidly from one gig to another.

“The question I kept asking myself was: Who’s that one person in the child’s life who’s not going to turn away, and is able to be with them to deliver that care?” Nguyen said. “Parents were always willing to raise their hand and step up. They would consistently ask us: Is there a way for me to learn these skills? So, I thought: Could we design a care model where the person who wants to deliver care to the patient is already with them?”

The answer was Abby Care, an AI-native home care startup that trains family members to become certified, paid caregivers and supports them thereafter. Nguyen founded the company—which operates as a Medicaid provider—in 2022.

Now, Abby Care has raised an $82 million Series C, led by Transformation Capital, Fortune has exclusively learned. CVS Health Ventures, Frist Cressey Ventures, and Pivotal Ventures count among the company’s new investors, while existing investors Khosla Ventures, Thrive Capital, and Sequoia doubled down. The company works with health plans to arrange care at home for families that need it. In short, the hope is that by looping in patients, regulators, health plans, and family caregivers, there’s a view toward a health care system that works better for the most vulnerable.

“The companies that are really going to be able to succeed are companies that can think about designing the care model that brings all the stakeholders and the U.S. health care system together,” Nguyen said.

Much has been made of the pressures on the health care workforce in the U.S., from the burnout of doctors and nurses to the extant and looming labor shortages. The caregiving gap for patients at home is notably wide, said Justin Brock, general partner at CVS Health Ventures. Brock noted there are many possible competitors to Abby Care, from existing home health agencies to caregiver education platforms, but the need is simply massive.

“A traditional private duty nurse program only fills 65% of authorized shifts, which is crazy,” he told Fortune. “It’s really leaving so many medically complex members without consistent coverage… [Meanwhile] you have these tens of millions of family caregivers who are in the home, and a lot of them are already doing care.”

Among them, Maria Villegas Corrales, a mom in Colorado, whose daughter Mia was born with serious medical complexities that necessitated open heart surgery and a pacemaker in the first years of her life. She learned about Abby Care after Mia’s surgery in June 2024, and Corrales is clear: Guidance isn’t a given.

“Sometimes they just give you a little bag to go home and figure it out,” Corrales said. “It’s scary to go home and not be able to know what’s to be expected. And a lot of times it’s just learning on the run.”

Corrales said that becoming a paid caregiver has allowed her to be the best mother possible to Mia, and that a lot of families still have no idea: “Families can have the resources to be paid to care for their child, that’s number one, because a lot of people don’t know about this.”

It’s a lifelong relationship, of course, which Nguyen is attuned to.

“I always tell the team this: Abby Care isn’t just here to empower and pay family caregivers,” she said. “We’re ultimately here to make them feel like they can thrive and succeed.”

items.title: Allium: stablecoin payments rose 45% YoY to $482B YTD through September 30, with transactions up 71% to 1.04B, while circulating supply grew just 0.4% (Krisztian Sandor/CoinDesk)
items.title_en: Allium: stablecoin payments rose 45% YoY to $482B YTD through September 30, with transactions up 71% to 1.04B, while circulating supply grew just 0.4% (Krisztian Sandor/CoinDesk)
items.author: CoinDesk
items.article_content:
Stablecoin supply has barely budged this year, but the digital dollars already in circulation are doing more work in payments, according to a fresh report from blockchain analytics firm Allium.

Stablecoin payments are growing at a rapid pace, reaching $482 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 45% from a year earlier, the report found.

That growth contrasts with the broader stablecoin market. The total value of stablecoins — cryptocurrencies tied to fiat currencies such as the U.S. dollar — in circulation stood at about $305 billion at the end of September, up a meager 0.4% since the start of the year, according to the report.

The number of payments grew even more, jumping 71% to over 1 billion, the report said, suggesting that stablecoins are changing hands more often without much new supply entering the market.

Stablecoin-linked cards showed some of the fastest growth. Spending measured by Allium reached $3.9 billion through September, ten times the amount a year earlier. Small purchases — under $50 — accounted for 84% of the increase in card transactions.

Three announcements earlier this week offered a glimpse of how stablecoins are becoming increasingly part of global payments.

Mastercard (MA) introduced Thursday its Global Money Platform with BVNK, the stablecoin infrastructure firm it acquired in August. The service combines traditional currency accounts, stablecoin balances, conversions, card spending and bank payouts through one connection.

Banks and fintechs can use the platform to offer accounts that hold both fiat currencies and stablecoins, the firm said. Payments firms Nuvei and Marqeta are among the first customers integrating that service.

Stripe, meanwhile, is working with Plasma XPL$0.07875, a blockchain-based financial services firm, on cards that support balances in dollars, euros, Brazilian reais, Mexican pesos and Colombian pesos, alongside eligible stablecoins.

The companies said they plan to let customers spend from the balance that matches their purchase, cutting unnecessary currency conversions. Stripe's expanded card infrastructure covers more than 30 countries, with plans to reach over 100 by next year.

And Visa (V) said it is bringing stablecoins into the funding side of international payments.

The company said Inyo Global, a payment orchestration firm for fintech, money transmitter, banks, became the first provider to put Visa Direct's stablecoin prefunding service into commercial use. Payment firms can use Circle's (CRCL) dollar stablecoin USDC USDC$1.0003 to fund cross-border payouts in nearly real-time instead of waiting for traditional banking windows, while recipients can still receive money through conventional payment channels.

That rapid growth of stablecoin payments comes with some caveats. Of $97.9 trillion in raw stablecoin transfers through September, Allium classified just $2.4 trillion, or 2.5%, as end-user activity after filtering out exchange, decentralized finance and automated transactions. Its $482 billion payments estimate comes from that smaller pool, the report said.

Stablecoin cards also remain a tiny fraction of conventional payments. Allium estimated that second-quarter spending through those cards amounted to just 0.03% of Visa's $4 trillion in payment volume.

For payment companies, that leaves a large market to pursue. Nuvei CEO Phil Fayer, whose company is among the first to integrate Mastercard's new platform, said stablecoins are becoming part of how businesses move money across borders and currencies.

"The future of global commerce depends on money moving as freely as the businesses and consumers it serves, across borders, currencies and increasingly, between traditional and digital forms of money," Fayer said.

The recent efforts by Mastercard, Stripe and Visa to incorporate stablecoins on blockchain rails reinforce that trend. Companies increasingly want stablecoins integrated into their existing financial operations, instead of running separate systems for digital assets, according to Patrick Mollard, co-founder and CEO of Paris-based Fipto, a stablecoin-powered business payments firm.

“The distinction between 'traditional' and 'digital' money is less important than giving businesses the ability to use whichever rail makes most sense for a particular payment or treasury operation,” he said in a note shared with CoinDesk.

“Businesses don't want separate crypto infrastructure sitting alongside their existing financial operations,” Mollard said. “They want to move between fiat and stablecoins within the same payments and treasury environment.”

The number of payments grew even more, jumping 71% to over 1 billion, the report said, suggesting that stablecoins are changing hands more often without much new supply entering the market.

Stablecoin-linked cards showed some of the fastest growth. Spending measured by Allium reached $3.9 billion through September, ten times the amount a year earlier. Small purchases — under $50 — accounted for 84% of the increase in card transactions.

Three announcements earlier this week offered a glimpse of how stablecoins are becoming increasingly part of global payments.

Mastercard (MA) introduced Thursday its Global Money Platform with BVNK, the stablecoin infrastructure firm it acquired in August. The service combines traditional currency accounts, stablecoin balances, conversions, card spending and bank payouts through one connection.

Banks and fintechs can use the platform to offer accounts that hold both fiat currencies and stablecoins, the firm said. Payments firms Nuvei and Marqeta are among the first customers integrating that service.

Stripe, meanwhile, is working with Plasma XPL$0.07875, a blockchain-based financial services firm, on cards that support balances in dollars, euros, Brazilian reais, Mexican pesos and Colombian pesos, alongside eligible stablecoins.

The companies said they plan to let customers spend from the balance that matches their purchase, cutting unnecessary currency conversions. Stripe's expanded card infrastructure covers more than 30 countries, with plans to reach over 100 by next year.

And Visa (V) said it is bringing stablecoins into the funding side of international payments.

The company said Inyo Global, a payment orchestration firm for fintech, money transmitter, banks, became the first provider to put Visa Direct's stablecoin prefunding service into commercial use. Payment firms can use Circle's (CRCL) dollar stablecoin USDC USDC$1.0003 to fund cross-border payouts in nearly real-time instead of waiting for traditional banking windows, while recipients can still receive money through conventional payment channels.

That rapid growth of stablecoin payments comes with some caveats. Of $97.9 trillion in raw stablecoin transfers through September, Allium classified just $2.4 trillion, or 2.5%, as end-user activity after filtering out exchange, decentralized finance and automated transactions. Its $482 billion payments estimate comes from that smaller pool, the report said.

Stablecoin cards also remain a tiny fraction of conventional payments. Allium estimated that second-quarter spending through those cards amounted to just 0.03% of Visa's $4 trillion in payment volume.

For payment companies, that leaves a large market to pursue. Nuvei CEO Phil Fayer, whose company is among the first to integrate Mastercard's new platform, said stablecoins are becoming part of how businesses move money across borders and currencies.

"The future of global commerce depends on money moving as freely as the businesses and consumers it serves, across borders, currencies and increasingly, between traditional and digital forms of money," Fayer said.

The recent efforts by Mastercard, Stripe and Visa to incorporate stablecoins on blockchain rails reinforce that trend. Companies increasingly want stablecoins integrated into their existing financial operations, instead of running separate systems for digital assets, according to Patrick Mollard, co-founder and CEO of Paris-based Fipto, a stablecoin-powered business payments firm.

“The distinction between 'traditional' and 'digital' money is less important than giving businesses the ability to use whichever rail makes most sense for a particular payment or treasury operation,” he said in a note shared with CoinDesk.

“Businesses don't want separate crypto infrastructure sitting alongside their existing financial operations,” Mollard said. “They want to move between fiat and stablecoins within the same payments and treasury environment.”

The GPU, called Intel GPU D-series and previously known by its Crescent Island codename, also hosts specialized computing hardware.

The Intel D-series has now dethroned Nvidia's Blackwell Ultra B300, which offers 288GB of HBM3e memory, as the data center GPU with the highest memory capacity.

Rather than using GDDR7 memory associated with modern graphics cards, Intel has chosen LPDDR5X, a memory technology commonly found in laptops and other power-conscious devices.

The configuration suggests that Intel is prioritizing memory capacity and power efficiency for AI inference instead of designing a conventional gaming graphics card.

Nvidia uses a memory 'sandwich' technique to cram 84GB GDDR7 memory on RTX Pro 5500 Blackwell GPU —  weird 416-bit memory bus leaves me puzzled, though
                    
                
                            
                    
                            
    
    
    
                        Chinese vendor debuts world's first AMD Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495 laptop, but 192GB LPDDR5X-8533 for gaming? Really??
                    
                
                            
                    
                            
    
    
    
                        This AI SSD tech makes 8 RTX 5090s perform like 46 GPUs in inference
                    
                
                    
    Intel says the accelerator can support large language models containing up to 300 billion parameters on one card, while an eight-GPU system can accommodate models exceeding one trillion parameters.

These capabilities are intended for lengthy prompts, simultaneous inference requests, enterprise AI services, and robotics applications requiring responsive processing.

“Inference is becoming the defining AI workload, and enterprises need infrastructure that delivers the right performance at the right cost,” said Anil Nanduri, vice president, AI Products & GTM, Intel Data Center Group.

“With Intel GPU D-series, we're focused on making high-capacity inference practical to deploy and economical to scale.”

The 480GB capacity is particularly relevant when AI systems must keep substantial model weights and associated data accessible during inference.

Thunderobot just launched a laptop that uses a special RAM-like SSD to boost AI performance — AI Master M7000 packs Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with 64GB RAM, runs 120B MoE models
                    
                
                            
                    
                            
    
    
    
                        HP debuts $7,449 Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 laptop — ZBook Ultra G3a has 192GB RAM, 512GB SSD, and can handle up to 300B parameters
                    
                
                            
                    
                            
    
    
    
                        Startup swaps costly AI GPUs for Arm cores and up to 128TB of 'cheap' LPDDR6 RAM instead of expensive HBM to smash through the memory wall
                    
                
                    
    However, memory capacity alone does not establish how quickly a GPU will serve requests, since performance also depends on bandwidth, computing resources, software, and workload characteristics.

Intel rates the D-series at 1.3 petaflops for FP8 computation, a numerical format commonly used to accelerate AI operations while reducing memory requirements compared with higher-precision formats.

Its 1.5TB/s memory bandwidth provides a separate measure of how quickly data can move between memory and the processor.

The company specifies a 350W power envelope and a standard PCIe form factor, alongside air cooling and software compatibility across its GPU platforms.

These characteristics are intended to simplify deployment in existing data centers without requiring specialized cooling arrangements or entirely new rack infrastructure.

Intel also plans to connect the accelerator with its Xeon processors, allowing CPUs to coordinate tasks, manage data movement, and handle workloads that do not require GPU acceleration.

This approach addresses AI systems increasingly built around multiple stages, including retrieval, reasoning, orchestration, external tools, and execution.

“Open models are expanding the options enterprises have for deploying AI,” said Nicolas Dubé, corporate vice president, Data Center Systems and Solutions Group, Intel.

“To realize their full potential, organizations need infrastructure that can match different workloads with the right intelligence, right compute resources and right economics. That's what we mean by 'put every prompt in its place.”

As of the time of writing, Intel has not revealed the public retail price or a specific general-availability date for the GPU D-series.

The GPU, called Intel GPU D-series and previously known by its Crescent Island codename, also hosts specialized computing hardware.

The Intel D-series has now dethroned Nvidia's Blackwell Ultra B300, which offers 288GB of HBM3e memory, as the data center GPU with the highest memory capacity.

Rather than using GDDR7 memory associated with modern graphics cards, Intel has chosen LPDDR5X, a memory technology commonly found in laptops and other power-conscious devices.

The configuration suggests that Intel is prioritizing memory capacity and power efficiency for AI inference instead of designing a conventional gaming graphics card.

Nvidia uses a memory 'sandwich' technique to cram 84GB GDDR7 memory on RTX Pro 5500 Blackwell GPU —  weird 416-bit memory bus leaves me puzzled, though
                    
                
                            
                    
                            
    
    
    
                        Chinese vendor debuts world's first AMD Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 495 laptop, but 192GB LPDDR5X-8533 for gaming? Really??
                    
                
                            
                    
                            
    
    
    
                        This AI SSD tech makes 8 RTX 5090s perform like 46 GPUs in inference
                    
                
                    
    Intel says the accelerator can support large language models containing up to 300 billion parameters on one card, while an eight-GPU system can accommodate models exceeding one trillion parameters.

These capabilities are intended for lengthy prompts, simultaneous inference requests, enterprise AI services, and robotics applications requiring responsive processing.

“Inference is becoming the defining AI workload, and enterprises need infrastructure that delivers the right performance at the right cost,” said Anil Nanduri, vice president, AI Products & GTM, Intel Data Center Group.

“With Intel GPU D-series, we're focused on making high-capacity inference practical to deploy and economical to scale.”

The 480GB capacity is particularly relevant when AI systems must keep substantial model weights and associated data accessible during inference.

Thunderobot just launched a laptop that uses a special RAM-like SSD to boost AI performance — AI Master M7000 packs Ryzen AI Max+ 395 with 64GB RAM, runs 120B MoE models
                    
                
                            
                    
                            
    
    
    
                        HP debuts $7,449 Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 laptop — ZBook Ultra G3a has 192GB RAM, 512GB SSD, and can handle up to 300B parameters
                    
                
                            
                    
                            
    
    
    
                        Startup swaps costly AI GPUs for Arm cores and up to 128TB of 'cheap' LPDDR6 RAM instead of expensive HBM to smash through the memory wall
                    
                
                    
    However, memory capacity alone does not establish how quickly a GPU will serve requests, since performance also depends on bandwidth, computing resources, software, and workload characteristics.

Intel rates the D-series at 1.3 petaflops for FP8 computation, a numerical format commonly used to accelerate AI operations while reducing memory requirements compared with higher-precision formats.

Its 1.5TB/s memory bandwidth provides a separate measure of how quickly data can move between memory and the processor.

The company specifies a 350W power envelope and a standard PCIe form factor, alongside air cooling and software compatibility across its GPU platforms.

These characteristics are intended to simplify deployment in existing data centers without requiring specialized cooling arrangements or entirely new rack infrastructure.

Intel also plans to connect the accelerator with its Xeon processors, allowing CPUs to coordinate tasks, manage data movement, and handle workloads that do not require GPU acceleration.

This approach addresses AI systems increasingly built around multiple stages, including retrieval, reasoning, orchestration, external tools, and execution.

“Open models are expanding the options enterprises have for deploying AI,” said Nicolas Dubé, corporate vice president, Data Center Systems and Solutions Group, Intel.

“To realize their full potential, organizations need infrastructure that can match different workloads with the right intelligence, right compute resources and right economics. That's what we mean by 'put every prompt in its place.”

As of the time of writing, Intel has not revealed the public retail price or a specific general-availability date for the GPU D-series.

items.title: China's GDP is set to grow 4.5% YoY in Q3, up from Q2's three-year-low growth rate of 4.3%, as AI-driven exports helped offset weak domestic spending (Osmond Chia/BBC)
items.title_en: China's GDP is set to grow 4.5% YoY in Q3, up from Q2's three-year-low growth rate of 4.3%, as AI-driven exports helped offset weak domestic spending (Osmond Chia/BBC)
items.author: BBC
items.article_content:
The world's second largest economy grew by 4.5% in the third quarter, up from the previous period but below the 5% expansion recorded from January to March, according to official Chinese data.

The latest figure is at the bottom end of Beijing's annual growth target of 4.5%-5%, which analysts have said gives policymakers room to address the country's economic challenges.

While exports have helped offset weak spending at home, global trade tensions and uncertainty over AI investments are clouding its outlook.

China's National Bureau of Statistics said on Monday that the economy "sustained steady development against pressure" and showed "momentum with new growth drivers and improving structure".

With exports climbing, China's trade surplus - the amount of goods and services it sells abroad compared to what it buys from other countries - is on track to overtake the record $1.2tn (£900bn) seen last year.

But property investment fell by more than 20% in the first nine months from the same period last year, official data also showed.

Oxford Economics researcher Sheana Yue said manufacturing and high-tech exports have boosted China's growth, despite weak investment and domestic spending.

China's economy has struggling to shake off a long-running property slump, after years of overbuilding and excessive borrowing by private developers.

There are still no signs that this trend will end soon, Yue said.

Trade uncertainties and geopolitical issues have also made Chinese consumers more "pessimistic" and unwilling to spend, she added.

The technology industry has been a key driver of China's growth in recent quarters.

Global demand for computer chips and other components used to build AI data centres has helped to ease pressure on Beijing and cushion the impact of sluggish domestic consumption.

Chinese businesses have leaned heavily on exports as a prolonged property slump, weak wage growth and high youth unemployment have weighed on consumer spending at home.

In September, Beijing unveiled a raft of support measures, including lower interest rates for some businesses and subsidies for property buyers, in an effort to boost the economy.

But Beijing is facing a backlash from Western economies - including the US and European Union - as manufacturers struggle to compete with large amounts of cheap Chinese goods.

There are also concerns over the billions of dollars being spent on AI infrastructure and whether the companies making those investments can deliver on their promises of generating huge profits.

Trading standards officers say AI is "super-charging" existing scams through clones and fake websites.

Tech firm Nscale says it is still committed to building the site in Essex.

The latest figure is at the bottom end of Beijing's annual growth target of 4.5%-5%, which analysts have said gives policymakers room to address the country's economic challenges.

While exports have helped offset weak spending at home, global trade tensions and uncertainty over AI investments are cloudin
items.summary_en: Economic growth rebounded slightly to 4.5% year-over-year in the third quarter from a three-year low of 4.3%, remaining at the bottom end of the official target. Strong exports driven by AI infrastructure and high-tech manufacturing helped offset a steep 20% drop in domestic real estate investment and subdued consumer spending, propelling the annual trade surplus toward new record highs.
items.title_zh: 三季度经济增长企稳微升硬科技出口对冲内需疲态
items.summary_zh: 三季度国内经济同比增长4.5%，受硬科技与AI出口拉动从低谷回暖，但内需承压仍面临下限考验

items.title: Sam Altman's World launches a World ID verification suite for banks, bundling tools to verify human and agent identities, its first industry-specific offering (Zack Abrams/The Block)
items.title_en: Sam Altman's World launches a World ID verification suite for banks, bundling tools to verify human and agent identities, its first industry-specific offering (Zack Abrams/The Block)
items.author: The Block
items.original_content:
Zack Abrams / The Block:
Sam Altman's World launches a World ID verification suite for banks, bundling tools to verify human and agent identities, its first industry-specific offering  —  The identity project co-founded by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman named Bain Capital
items.content_snippet: The identity project co-founded by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman named Bain Capital and VanEck Funds among its design partners but did not name …
items.summary_en: Sam Altman's World project introduced its first enterprise-specific verification suite tailored for the banking sector, bundling tools to distinguish real humans from autonomous AI agents. Aiming to tackle mounting deepfake financial fraud and evolving agentic transactions, the initiative seeks to integrate its proprietary proof-of-humanhood credentials directly into institutional financial risk infrastructures.
items.title_zh: 奥特曼旗下身份认证体系针对银行业推专用套件
items.summary_zh: 奥特曼旗下项目推出银行业专属身份套件，打包真人与自主代理识别能力，开启金融变现

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 由山姆·奥特曼联合创立的数字身份认证项目在金融合规场景中迈出商业化关键一步，正式针对全球银行与金融机构推出了首款行业级定制套件。该产品组合专门打包了区分真实人类生物特征与自主AI智能体身份的核查能力，并已吸引到主流顶级风险投资机构的落地协同。随着深度伪造与自主智能代理对传统远程客户核验系统造成系统性冲击，该项目试图将其饱受争议的虹膜和人证链条植入全球金融风控大门，完成从实验性加密项目到主流金融基础设施的蜕变。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Sam Altman's World project introduced its first enterprise-specific verification suite tailored for the banking sector, bundling tools to distinguish real humans from autonomous AI agents. Aiming to tackle mounting deepfake financial fraud and evolving agentic transactions, the initiative seeks to integrate its proprietary proof-of-humanhood credentials directly into institutional financial risk infrastructures.

elements_zh.who: 山姆·奥特曼及其联合创立的 World 机构
elements_zh.where: 全球商业银行与金融机构合规反欺诈场景
elements_zh.what: 发布首个面向银行业的 World ID 身份验证套件，捆绑真人与AI代理鉴别工具
elements_zh.why: 利用深度伪造泛滥和自主AI代理兴起对银行传统KYC防线造成的危机，加速向机构端商业化渗透

elements_en.who: Sam Altman and co-founded project World
elements_en.where: Global retail banking and institutional compliance environments
elements_en.what: Rolled out its first industry-specific verification suite allowing banks to verify humans and autonomous agents
elements_en.why: Capitalizes on deepfake risks and autonomous bot commerce breaking traditional banking KYC systems

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 奥特曼不仅亲手让大模型把深伪假人和AI脚本卷到了足以把银行风控逼疯的程度，转头就掏出自己的虹膜认证设备去敲银行的门兜售“防伪防骗解药”。这种左手制造AI信任危机、右手垄断数字验明正身的自产自销闭环，把硅谷科技狂人的算盘珠子都直接崩到了华尔街脸上。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Altman first unleashed generative AI and autonomous bots capable of driving banking fraud detectors to the brink of insanity, only to turn right around and sell banks the iris-scanning antidote. Inventing the crisis on one side of the street and selling the identity passport on the other is peak Silicon Valley arbitrage that leaves Wall Street with no choice but to pay up.

items.title: Analysis: 795 accounts funded by ADI Predictstreet's own fee-collecting wallet drove 99% of the FIFA-partnered prediction market's activity since late August (Wall Street Journal)
items.title_en: Analysis: 795 accounts funded by ADI Predictstreet's own fee-collecting wallet drove 99% of the FIFA-partnered prediction market's activity since late August (Wall Street Journal)
items.author: Wall Street Journal
items.original_content:
Wall Street Journal:
Analysis: 795 accounts funded by ADI Predictstreet's own fee-collecting wallet drove 99% of the FIFA-partnered prediction market's activity since late August  —  ADI Predictstreet, backed by Abu Dhabi's royal family, paid close to $150 million
items.content_snippet: ADI Predictstreet, backed by Abu Dhabi's royal family, paid close to $150 million for advertising rights during the World Cup
items.summary_en: On-chain analysis revealed that 795 accounts directly funded by the platform's own fee-collecting wallet generated 99% of all trading activity on ADI Predictstreet since late August. Backed by Abu Dhabi royal family funds, the prediction market recently splashed nearly $150 million on a FIFA partnership, using wash trading to fabricate massive liquidity and cover up the glaring lack of genuine organic user interest.
items.title_zh: 体育预测平台被曝左手倒右手 官方小号刷出近全部交易额
items.summary_zh: 斥资近1.5亿美元签约国际足联的预测市场平台被曝严重刷量，超九成交易活动由官方收费钱包资助的账户对敲制造
items.article_content_zh:
区块链链上交易追踪数据显示，与国际足联（FIFA）达成高额赞助合作的去中心化预测市场平台ADI Predictstreet存在极为严重的虚假交易与自我对敲现象。自8月下旬以来的所有投注记录中，有795个高度活跃的独立钱包账户直接由该平台归集用户手续费的官方主钱包提供运作资金，这批关联钱包主导了平台同期超过99%的成交量。

作为背靠阿布扎比王室资本的新兴预测产品，该机构此前承诺斥资近1.5亿美元与国际足联建立长期品牌合作，试图在全球大型体育赛事期间抢夺加密预测赛道的头把交椅。然而链上公开记录表明，除了这数百个官方资金支持的傀儡节点相互对冲买卖外，真实散户资金的流入和有效订单深度几乎可以忽略不计。

这一数据曝光再次将Web3与体育赛事IP巨额联名的实质成效推上风口浪尖。大量链上分析机构指出，在缺乏真实用户基础和产品合规落地场景的前提下，通过中心化资金池分流制造虚假流动性指标，已成为部分背靠雄厚资本的加密平台在对外公关宣传中粉饰估值、向商业伙伴交差的常规手段。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 由阿布扎比王室资本支持的预测市场平台ADI在豪掷近1.5亿美元拿下国际足联官方合作后，被链上数据深度剖析戳破繁荣泡沫。链上分析表明，该平台自8月下旬以来的交易额中，高达99%的活动均由官方手续费归集钱包直接注资的795个傀儡账户刷量产生。这一极端对敲行为旨在为主流体育机构入局Web3营造流动性充足与用户活跃的假象，掩盖高价赞助背后真实散户参与极度匮乏的尴尬现状。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: On-chain analysis revealed that 795 accounts directly funded by the platform's own fee-collecting wallet generated 99% of all trading activity on ADI Predictstreet since late August. Backed by Abu Dhabi royal family funds, the prediction market recently splashed nearly $150 million on a FIFA partnership, using wash trading to fabricate massive liquidity and cover up the glaring lack of genuine organic user interest.

elements_zh.where: Web3链上交易与国际体育赞助市场
elements_zh.what: 自8月下旬以来，由平台自身抽水钱包直接提供资金的795个账户，对冲刷出了平台99%的交易活动
elements_zh.why: 在耗费约1.5亿美元巨资签约国际足联后，平台极度缺乏真实散户与流动性，被迫自掏腰包制造虚假繁荣

elements_en.who: ADI Predictstreet, an Abu Dhabi royal-backed prediction market
elements_en.where: Web3 on-chain prediction markets and international sports sponsorship
elements_en.what: 795 accounts funded directly by the platform's own fee-collecting wallet drove 99% of trading activity since late August
elements_en.why: After committing nearly $150M to a FIFA partnership, the platform faced an embarrassing lack of real retail volume and resorted to wash trading to simulate user demand

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 花了1.5亿美元天价买下国际足联的门面，结果进场一看全是空气，只能官方开近800个小号在空旷的赌桌上左手倒右手。Web3世界最讽刺的剧本莫过于此：球赛比分是猜的，平台数据是编的，连坐在你对面的赌客都是官方按代码生成的NPC群演。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Dropping $150 million on a FIFA sponsorship only to face an empty room is peak crypto tragedy—so naturally, management spun up 800 sockpuppets to trade with themselves. The ultimate irony of Web3 prediction markets: the match outcome is a gamble, but you can always bet 99% of the players at the table are just company-funded bots.

items.title: Europe's three biggest industrial companies are cashing in on the AI boom, as Schneider and Siemens expand further into software, while ABB focuses on equipment (Aaron Kirchfeld/Financial Times)
items.title_en: Europe's three biggest industrial companies are cashing in on the AI boom, as Schneider and Siemens expand further into software, while ABB focuses on equipment (Aaron Kirchfeld/Financial Times)
items.author: Financial Times
items.original_content:
Aaron Kirchfeld / Financial Times:
Europe's three biggest industrial companies are cashing in on the AI boom, as Schneider and Siemens expand further into software, while ABB focuses on equipment  —  Schneider Electric and Siemens move further into software as riv
items.content_snippet: Schneider Electric and Siemens move further into software as rival ABB bets on physical equipment
items.summary_en: Europe's top three industrial giants—Schneider Electric, Siemens, and ABB—are capitalizing on the global AI infrastructure surge with diverging playbooks. While Schneider and Siemens push aggressively into industrial software and energy automation, ABB doubles down on high-demand electrical equipment for data centers. The unprecedented power and compute demands of generative AI have turned these legacy titans into the primary beneficiaries of the ongoing tech boom.
items.title_zh: 欧洲三大工业巨头借人工智能热潮大赚特赚
items.summary_zh: 施耐德与西门子发力工业软件，ABB专攻电气装备，欧洲三大老牌巨头分食算力基建红利
items.article_content_zh:
随着生成式人工智能热潮推动超大规模数据中心建设，欧洲工业三巨头施耐德电气、西门子和ABB迎来了数十年来最迅猛的业务增长期。算力集群消耗的恐怖电量使电力基础设施成为AI竞赛的命门，这让长年深耕能源管理和自动化控制的欧洲制造巨头跃升为最吃香的“卖铲人”。

三大集团正在执行泾渭分明的技术变现路线。施耐德电气与西门子正全力将自身重塑为高毛利的工业软件巨头，通过收购和自研工业物联网平台、数字孪生及AI能耗调度软件，深度绑定数据中心运营商。相比之下，瑞士工程巨头ABB则坚定聚焦于电气化硬件，为超大规模机房交付大容量断路器、中低压配电柜和不间断电源等核心工业装备。

分析指出，大模型狂潮正引发全球电力供应紧缺与电网升级需求。无论科技巨头选择哪种模型架构，都必须依靠坚固的电网接入和精细的电力调优，这为掌控着配电标准与底层核心专利的欧洲老牌工业集团提供了长达数年的稳定利润护城河。

ai_analysis.insight_en: While Silicon Valley burns billions hallucinating future AGI profits, Europe's centenarian industrial titans are quietly laughing all the way to the bank. Whether peddling software suites or shipping heavy transformers, the AI hype cycle ultimately pays rent to the same electrical gatekeepers. The tech industry may not have figured out how to monetize LLMs yet, but the digital age's real landlords are already collecting their dues.

items.title: SF-based home insurer Stand, which uses digital twins of homes to price wildfire risk and insures $10B+ of property, raised a $70M Series C at a $1B valuation (Nick Lichtenberg/Fortune)
items.title_en: SF-based home insurer Stand, which uses digital twins of homes to price wildfire risk and insures $10B+ of property, raised a $70M Series C at a $1B valuation (Nick Lichtenberg/Fortune)
items.author: Fortune
items.article_content:
Removing one takes more than $1,100 a year off the home’s premium. Another, he says, “doesn’t contribute as much.”

“This one’s the one that matters,” DiStefano says of the first tree. He is Stand’s 29-year-old chief science officer and he’s demoing, via screen share, Stand’s proprietary digital twin technology that hopes to solve the insurance industry’s multibillion-dollar problem.

The San Francisco home insurer is announcing today a $70 million Series C raise at a $1 billion valuation, Fortune can exclusively reveal. Its argument is that insurers have been pricing wildfire risk the wrong way, by looking backward at statistics and sorting homes by zip code. Stand says the better approach is to simulate each house and show the owner what to fix.

Saga Ventures led the round, with participation from Lowercarbon, Eclipse, Equal Ventures, Inspired Capital, Neotribe, and Jackson Square Ventures, among others. Stand says it now insures more than $10 billion of property, up from $1 billion a year ago. CEO Dan Preston says the business is growing about 15% a month, and that it has done so in only two states: in California for wildfire and in Florida for hurricanes.

DiStefano’s critique of the industry is that a zip-code model gives a homeowner a score that works like a credit score, but there’s nothing they do can move it. He said insurers can barely tell apart two homes on the same block. His illustration is a windowless brick bunker with nothing around it set beside a wooden shed with a thatched roof. “Logically, that home can’t burn,” and yet a location-based model treats the two alike.

The result, DiStefano said, is homeowners who spend tens of thousands of dollars hardening their houses and still get non-renewed. He said they have heard “hundreds of stories” like that from clients describing their experience before engaging with Stand.

Stand builds what it calls a digital twin of each home. “We simulate what would happen if an event happened, so if a wildfire occurred or if a tropical cyclone occurred,” DiStefano said. “We’re not looking at the neighboring home. We’re looking at this specific home, the specific materials and the specific arrangement of trees.” The model also accounts for wind direction and weather conditions, he said.

The 29-year-old DiStefano spent years in aerospace, at companies “some as large as Boeing, others were small YC startups,” building “models of circuit boards and satellites and simulating how they would react in orbit.” What was new at Stand, he said, was “applying it to something that was so much more tangible for hundreds of millions of people.”

Stand runs computational fluid dynamics, physics models built on top of digital twins. DiStefano likened it to work that you would do while designing an airplane (he has stints at Boeing and SpaceX on his CV). DiStefano argued that Stand is bringing a new level of detailed analysis to the insurance industry. Each digital twin consists of layers of site information accounting for the home structure, surroundings, and details such as trees, brush, wind direction and weather.

The company said it has also developed an in-house frontier AI, the Stand World Model, which understands physics and allows it to run simulations instantaneously. DiStefano said they “successfully taught neural networks to actually understand the physics.” That’s why he can delete a tree on screen and watch the price move.

DiStefano said Stand tested the model from a blind, forward-looking validation against actual outcomes for roughly 310 California homes that experienced wildfires over the past three to four years, including homes affected by the Palisades Fire.

The model was run as if it had no knowledge of what happened, DiStefano explained, and it predicted burn or survival about 85% of the time. He claimed that competing models, which add “secondary modifiers” like single-pane windows to a statistical base, got it right 50–55% of the time. The comparison figures were generated by evaluating industry standard location-based incumbent models against the same cohort and measuring whether they correctly distinguished burned from surviving homes.

Competitive models “really are a coin flip,” DiStefano said, arguing that this is why rates rise across the board after a disaster, and why customers get dropped seemingly at random. (The results are Stand’s own, and Fortune could not independently verify them.)

DiStefano said the model has rated some homes as having a 99.8% chance of being lost in a fire, and that targeted changes recommended by Stand’s model have brought that close to 15%.

CEO and co-founder Dan Preston said the company’s structure follows from this model, as it actively helps customers redesign their properties around DiStefano’s simulations, a function that didn’t exist before.

“We literally have somebody on staff who used to be a construction builder,” Preston said.

Preston, 41, was previously CEO at Metromile, the pay-per-mile auto insurer, before starting Stand about two-and-a-half years ago. “Disasters follow the laws of physics, and insurance should too,” Preston said in a statement. Stand sells through brokers, and Preston said it now works with the country’s largest.

Co-founder and chief product officer Jason Mueller said one of Stand’s “biggest secrets” is making brokers “look like heroes,” with near-instant quotes and a platform that replaces trading PDFs.

Mueller, who is 40, previously led product at Policygenius and said he has known Preston for about 17 years. He said his product and engineering team is about 10 people doing “100 times the work” of his last team of 100 or more, because modern AI tooling lets a small group build fast. The applied science team is about 10, as well.

Mueller said Stand has more in the works, such as financing the mitigation work over the life of a policy, letting real estate companies pre-underwrite their inventory, and letting a policy transfer to the next buyer of a home, although they aren’t in the short-term pipeline. “People often say, like, insurance is sold, not bought,” he said, adding that the company’s data on where it wins and loses deals is part of what it is building.

The last round, a Series B led by Eclipse, closed a little more than a year ago, and Preston said the company “hit our inflection point” soon afterward, and the new money mostly backs the growth that followed. It plans to expand across the wildfire-prone West and the Southeast, and later into regions exposed to severe convective storms, freezes and flooding.

Stand also announced two hires to run that expansion. Drew Saad, formerly chief underwriting officer at PURE Insurance, joins as president of property and casualty. Tony Landi, formerly head of strategic growth at Nephila and head of capital markets at Openly, becomes chief financial officer.

Stand’s policies are issued by Concert Specialty Insurance Company (AM Best A-) in California and by Stand Insurance Exchange (Demotech A) in Florida. Reinsurers include Arch, RenaissanceRe, Hannover, Nephila and Hiscox.

DiStefano grew up on Long Island and lived through Hurricane Sandy in high school, an experience that he said left him wanting to change how communities relate to the buildings around them. He said he first encountered digital twin technology in high school, when he built models of cancer cells reacting to drugs in a Mount Sinai lab. (Yes, he was literally trying to cure cancer before working to mitigate wildfires.) He said the common thread in his career has been applying models to “less highly engineered systems,” and a house is one of those.

DiStefano also draws on history. He said he is interested in 19th-century cities that burned and in how firefighting technology eventually solved the problem. “I see this as just the latest challenge among many challenges that society is facing and to solve it, we’re creating and deploying new technology.”

Nick Lichtenberg is business editor and was formerly Fortune's executive editor of global news.

items.summary_en: San Francisco-based home insurer Stand raised a $70 million Series C round led by Saga Ventures at a $1 billion valuation, officially reaching unicorn status. The company replaces legacy zip-code-based actuarial tables with 3D digital twins of individual homes to accurately model wildfire and hurricane risks, even showing homeowners how removing a specific tree can shave over $1,100 off annual premiums. elements_en.what: Secured a $70M Series C round led by Saga Ventures at a $1B valuation, reaching unicorn status while insuring $10B+ in property assets
elements_en.why: Traditional insurers are retreating from climate-risk zones using blunt zip-code models, while Stand leverages 3D digital twins to precisely price catastrophe risk and guide mitigation

ai_analysis.insight_en: While legacy insurance giants are busy fleeing disaster-prone states and hiking rates indiscriminately, Stand turned 3D modeling into a billion-dollar money printer. Telling a homeowner that chopping down one specific backyard tree saves $1,100 a year is the ultimate Silicon Valley sleight of hand: brilliantly shifting physical disaster-mitigation homework to the customer while charging them top dollar for the privilege of high-tech clarity.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 旧金山房屋保险科技公司Stand正式完成由Saga Ventures领投的7000万美元C轮融资，投后估值达到10亿美元成为新晋独角兽。该公司摒弃了传统保险业依据邮政编码粗放定保费的模式，利用3D数字孪生技术模拟单栋房屋在野火或飓风中的受灾路径，甚至能精确计算砍掉院子里哪棵特定树木即可立减上千美元保费。目前其业务已覆盖加州野火与佛州飓风重灾区，承保资产规模突破100亿美元，正以每月约15%的速度高速扩张。

items.title_en: Sources: Nscale faces investor pushback on its ~$30B IPO valuation, with some urging a lower valuation of $16B to $19B, as Microsoft exits a UK data center deal (Bailey Lipschultz/Bloomberg)
items.author: Bloomberg
items.original_content:
Bailey Lipschultz / Bloomberg:
Sources: Nscale faces investor pushback on its ~$30B IPO valuation, with some urging a lower valuation of $16B to $19B, as Microsoft exits a UK data center deal  —  Nscale Ltd. is facing opposition to the valuation target it's pursui
items.content_snippet: Nscale Ltd. is facing opposition to the valuation target it's pursuing in its initial public offering, according to people familiar …
items.summary_en: AI infrastructure provider Nscale is facing severe investor pushback against its targeted $30 billion IPO valuation. Following Microsoft's abrupt withdrawal from a major UK data center contract, investors are now urging the firm to slash its valuation expectations down to between $16 billion and $19 billion.
items.title_zh: 消息来源：随着微软退出一项英国数据中心交易，投资者对Nscale约300亿美元的IPO估值持反对态度，一些人认为估值应降至160亿至190亿美元。
items.summary_zh: Bailey Lipschultz / Bloomberg：消息来源：Nscale 面临投资者对其约 30B 美元 IPO 估值的阻力，随着微软退出英国数据中心交易，一些人敦促将估值降低至 16B 至 19B 美元 — Nscale Ltd. 面临对其追求的估值目标的反对

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 人工智能云基础设施提供商Nscale在推进首次公开募股进程中遭遇投资机构强烈阻力。由于大客户微软近期退出了其位于英国的一项关键数据中心合作交易，市场对其高估值的营收兑现能力产生动摇，承销与投资机构力主将其原定追求的300亿美元上市估值砍至160亿到190亿美元区间。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: AI infrastructure provider Nscale is facing severe investor pushback against its targeted $30 billion IPO valuation. Following Microsoft's abrupt withdrawal from a major UK data center contract, investors are now urging the firm to slash its valuation expectations down to between $16 billion and $19 billion.

items.title: Sources: industry execs expect only 7-10 of hundreds of neoclouds to survive, as Nvidia supports them with easier credit terms, site finding, and $20B in leases (Phoebe Liu/The Information)
items.title_en: Sources: industry execs expect only 7-10 of hundreds of neoclouds to survive, as Nvidia supports them with easier credit terms, site finding, and $20B in leases (Phoebe Liu/The Information)
items.author: The Information
items.original_content:
Phoebe Liu / The Information:
Sources: industry execs expect only 7-10 of hundreds of neoclouds to survive, as Nvidia supports them with easier credit terms, site finding, and $20B in leases  —  How many young AI cloud providers can the market, and Nvidia, support
items.content_snippet: How many young AI cloud providers can the market, and Nvidia, support? — That's one of the big questions after a week …
items.summary_en: Industry executives expect only 7 to 10 of the hundreds of emerging AI neoclouds to survive the ongoing shakeout. To prop up these struggling providers, Nvidia is intervening with relaxed credit terms, datacenter site selection assistance, and up to $20 billion in lease commitments. The move is aimed at preventing high-profile defaults while maintaining leverage against legacy hyperscalers who are building their own silicon.
items.title_zh: 消息来源：业内高管预计，数百家新云公司中只有7-10家能够存活下来，因为英伟达为它们提供了更容易的信贷条款、选址和200亿美元的租约。
items.summary_zh: Phoebe Liu / The Information：资料来源：行业高管预计数百个 Neocloud 中只有 7-10 个能够生存，因为 Nvidia 通过更轻松的信贷条件、站点查找和 200 亿美元的租赁来支持他们 - 市场和 Nvidia 可以支持多少年轻的 AI 云提供商

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 多位算力行业高管透露，在当前涌现的数百家新兴AI算力云服务商中，预计最终仅有7到10家能够逃脱倒闭宿命。芯片霸主英伟达为维系这一生态，正主动提供极度宽松的还款账期、协助寻找数据中心机房，并开出了高达200亿美元的设备租赁支持。英伟达此举旨在防止重度负债的中小算力商发生挤兑崩盘，同时通过扶持新兴第三方云，制衡微软、亚马逊等自研芯片日益成熟的传统云巨头。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Industry executives expect only 7 to 10 of the hundreds of emerging AI neoclouds to survive the ongoing shakeout. To prop up these struggling providers, Nvidia is intervening with relaxed credit terms, datacenter site selection assistance, and up to $20 billion in lease commitments. The move is aimed at preventing high-profile defaults while maintaining leverage against legacy hyperscalers who are building their own silicon.

elements_zh.where: 全球AI算力基础设施与云服务租赁市场
elements_zh.what: 行业预计绝大多数新兴算力云将淘汰出局，英伟达通过放宽信贷与200亿美元租赁进行定向输血扶持
elements_zh.why: 中小算力中间商陷入重资产高负债与空置率危机，英伟达必须托底护盘以防呆账暴雷，并借此抗衡自研芯片的三大传统云巨头

elements_en.where: Global AI cloud infrastructure and GPU leasing market
elements_en.what: Executives predict 90%+ neoclouds will fail, while Nvidia steps in with easy credit and $20B in lease support
elements_en.why: Capital-heavy neoclouds face cash crunches; Nvidia must prop them up to avert credit defaults and check hyperscaler dominance

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 黄仁勋这招堪称现代版‘左手卖铲子，右手借钱给淘金者付租金’。表面上是给算力创业小弟们送温暖，骨子里是生怕这帮击鼓传花的中间商暴雷砸了自家的逆天财报；更妙的是，养着这几条小鲶鱼，还能天天在微软和亚马逊的眼皮底下恶心他们‘别以为只有你们能买卡’。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Jensen Huang is basically loaning gold diggers money to lease his own shovels. Propping up these neoclouds isn't charity; it's preventative damage control against massive customer defaults and a calculated hedge to keep AWS and Microsoft from getting too cocky with their in-house chips.
